questions.question: How do you test Spring Security with @WithMockUser and SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors?
questions.title: Testing with @WithMockUser and SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors
questions.direct_answer: **`@WithMockUser`** populates the `SecurityContext` with a mock `Authentication` before the test method runs, simulating a logged-in user without going through the actual authentication flow. **`SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors`** (`user()`, `jwt()`, `csrf()`) apply mock security context **per-request** in MockMvc calls, giving finer control when different requests in the same test need different users. **`@WithUserDetails`** loads a real user from your `UserDetailsService` (tests the full path including account flags). For JWT Resource Server endpoints, **`jwt()`** post-processor creates the correct `JwtAuthenticationToken` (vs `@WithMockUser` which creates `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` — wrong type for `instanceof` checks).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the candidate knows how to write meaningful security tests without spinning up a real auth server.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using @WithMockUser without @AutoConfigureMockMvc, or testing method security without @SpringBootTest (which loads the AOP proxies).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss @WithUserDetails for testing with real UserDetailsService data, custom @WithMockCustomUser meta-annotations, and testing JWT resource servers with SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt().

sections.title: Security Testing Needs the Full Stack to Work
sections.content:
Security testing in Spring requires an application context that loads the security filter chain and its configuration.
- **`@WithMockUser` is not magic** — it populates the `SecurityContextHolder` before the test method runs, but only has an effect if a Spring context is processing it through `WithSecurityContextTestExecutionListener`.
- **On a plain JUnit test with no Spring context annotation, `@WithMockUser` silently does nothing.**

**For controller-level security testing** (URL-level rules, 401/403 responses, CSRF behavior), use **`@WebMvcTest`** with **`@AutoConfigureMockMvc`**. Loads security filter chain + MVC layer without full app context. Mock missing dependencies with `@MockBean`.

**For method-level security** (`@PreAuthorize`, `@PostAuthorize`), use **`@SpringBootTest`**.
- Method security requires AOP proxies, which only exist when full app context loads.
- Testing a `@PreAuthorize`-annotated service with `@WebMvcTest` calls the service through a mock — proxy doesn't exist, annotation has no effect, test passes when security is broken.

**Two testing approaches:**
- **Declarative**: `@WithMockUser` etc. set up context for entire test method
- **Imperative**: `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors` set up context per request — different users for different requests in same test

sections.title: @WithMockUser vs @WithUserDetails
SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt() for Resource Server
sections.content:
**Wrong type problem:**
- `@WithMockUser` creates `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken`
- JWT Resource Server endpoints use `JwtAuthenticationToken`
- Code that checks `instanceof JwtAuthenticationToken` or accesses `((JwtAuthenticationToken) auth).getToken()` -> `ClassCastException` with `@WithMockUser`

**`jwt()` post-processor — correct type for JWT endpoints:**

```java
import static org.springframework.security.test.web.servlet.request.SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt;

@Test
void adminJwtCanAccessProtectedEndpoint() throws Exception {
    mockMvc.perform(get("/api/admin/report")
        .with(jwt()
            .authorities(new SimpleGrantedAuthority("ROLE_ADMIN"))
            .jwt(jwtBuilder -> jwtBuilder
                .subject("user123")
                .claim("roles", List.of("ADMIN"))
                .claim("org_id", "org-456"))))
        .andExpect(status().isOk());
}

@Test
void missingAuthReturns401() throws Exception {
    mockMvc.perform(get("/api/admin/report"))
        .andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());
}
```

**What `jwt()` enables:**
- Set JWT claims precisely
- Control resulting `GrantedAuthority` list independently
- Test `JwtAuthenticationConverter` behavior: set raw claim, verify produced authority

**Other useful post-processors:**
- **`csrf()`** — provides valid CSRF token for state-changing requests
- **`user("alice").roles("ADMIN")`** — quick mock without annotation
- **`anonymous()`** — explicit anonymous principal
- **`oauth2Login()`** — mock OAuth2 login user
- **`opaqueToken()`** — mock opaque token (for introspection-based resource server)

**Verifying unauthenticated returns 401, not 403:**
- 401 = not authenticated
- 403 = authenticated but lacks required authority
- Distinguish to ensure security config matches intent

sections.title: Custom Security Test Annotations
Method Security and What @WithMockUser Can't Test
Security Testing: Helps, Hurts, Watch For
sections.content:
**When `@WithMockUser` helps:**
- Fast — no DB, no UserDetailsService call
- Declarative — clear intent at method level
- Perfect for authorization rule testing

**When `@WithUserDetails` helps:**
- Tests real user loading + account flags
- Custom `UserDetails` properties used by authorization
- End-to-end of `loadUserByUsername` -> authority mapping

**When `jwt()` post-processor helps:**
- Resource Server endpoints (correct token type)
- Per-request precision
- Testing claim-to-authority mapping logic

**When custom annotations help:**
- Large suites (50+ tests with same user setup)
- JWT/OIDC tokens with custom claim shapes
- Centralized changes to test user definition

**When it hurts:**
- `@WithMockUser` + JWT endpoint -> ClassCastException on `JwtAuthenticationToken`
- `@WithMockUser` without `@WebMvcTest`/`@SpringBootTest` -> silently no-op
- Method security test without `@EnableMethodSecurity` -> tests always pass
- Forgetting `csrf()` post-processor on POST/PUT/DELETE -> 403 not from auth but from CSRF

**Watch for:**
- **Silent no-op** — `@WithMockUser` on plain JUnit without Spring context
- **Wrong token type** — `@WithMockUser` for JWT endpoints
- **Missing `csrf()`** — state-changing requests fail with 403 unrelated to auth
- **`@WebMvcTest` + method security** — AOP proxies not loaded; annotation tests pass falsely
- **Test DB pollution** — `@WithUserDetails` mutates state; reset between tests
- **`SecurityContextHolder` leakage** — if a test sets it manually, clear in `@AfterEach`
- **401 vs 403** — distinguish in assertions; mixing them hides config errors
- **`MockMvc` not security-configured** — needs `@AutoConfigureMockMvc` (auto in `@WebMvcTest`)
- **OAuth2 login tests** — use `oauth2Login()` post-processor, not `@WithMockUser`

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **`@WithMockUser` sets a `SecurityContext` without loading `UserDetailsService`** — fake `Authentication` with username/roles/authorities; no DB.
- **`@AutoConfigureMockMvc` or `@WebMvcTest` is required for `MockMvc` to apply security** — without it, security filter chain is not applied.
- **`@WithUserDetails("alice")` loads a real user from `UserDetailsService`** — tests full auth path including account flags.
- **Test `@PreAuthorize` on services with `@WithMockUser` + `@SpringBootTest`** — `@WebMvcTest` doesn't load AOP proxies for method security.
- **`SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt()`** for Resource Server endpoints — correct token type, claim precision.
- **Custom `@WithMockJwtUser` via `@WithSecurityContext`** — reusable across suite, centralized changes.
- **Always include `csrf()`** for POST/PUT/DELETE in CSRF-enabled chains.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**`@WithMockUser` — fast path**
- Creates `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` in `SecurityContext`
- No `UserDetailsService` call
- Perfect for authorization rule testing: 'does ROLE_USER get 403 here?'
- Does not test the authentication flow itself

**`@WithUserDetails` — full path**
- Calls `loadUserByUsername("alice")` on real `UserDetailsService`
- Tests user loading, account flags, real `UserDetails` shape
- Requires alice to exist in test DB

**MockMvc setup**
- `@WebMvcTest` -> auto-configures MockMvc with security filter chain
- `@SpringBootTest + @AutoConfigureMockMvc` -> full context for method security

**Resource Server JWT testing**
- Use `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt()` for correct `JwtAuthenticationToken` type
- Set claims precisely
- Test `JwtAuthenticationConverter` behavior

**Custom annotations for large suites**
- `@WithMockAdmin` meta-annotation
- `@WithMockJwtUser` with `WithSecurityContextFactory`
- One change updates all tests

**Common mistakes**
- `@WithMockUser` on plain JUnit -> silent no-op
- `@WithMockUser` for JWT endpoint -> ClassCastException
- `@WebMvcTest` + method security -> false positives
- Missing `csrf()` post-processor on state-changing requests

questions.question: How do you write end-to-end MockMvc tests with Spring Security, including method-level security and CSRF?
questions.title: MockMvc with Spring Security: End-to-End and Method Security Testing
questions.direct_answer: End-to-end MockMvc security tests require **`@WebMvcTest`** (or `@SpringBootTest` + `@AutoConfigureMockMvc`) so the **`SecurityFilterChain`** is wired into the `MockMvc` instance via **`SecurityMockMvcConfigurers.springSecurity()`** (auto-applied with `@WebMvcTest`). Use **`with(csrf())`** for state-changing requests in CSRF-enabled chains. **Method-level security** (`@PreAuthorize`/`@PostAuthorize`) needs `@SpringBootTest` because it depends on AOP proxies that `@WebMvcTest` does not create — use `@EnableMethodSecurity` and assert `AccessDeniedException`. For each rule, write a **positive** test (allowed role -> 2xx) and a **negative** test (wrong role -> 403, no auth -> 401). Verify the security context with **`SecurityMockMvcResultMatchers.authenticated()`** and `.withAuthorities(...)`.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether the candidate can structure a real security test suite that catches regressions, not a happy-path smoke test.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Testing controllers with @WebMvcTest while expecting @PreAuthorize annotations on services to fire — they do not, because the proxy isn't created.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss negative tests as first-class citizens, custom @WithSecurityContext factories for JWT, integration tests with Testcontainers Keycloak, and the @WebMvcTest vs @SpringBootTest decision matrix.

sections.title: End-to-End Security Testing — Beyond the Smoke Test
sections.content:
Most production security regressions come from missing **negative tests**.
- A test that calls `/admin/users` with an admin token and gets `200` proves the happy path works — but says nothing about whether a regular user is rejected, whether an unauthenticated request is rejected, or whether method-level rules fire.
- **A real security test suite has at least two tests per rule**: one positive, one negative.

**MockMvc is the right tool for this** — it's fast, doesn't require a running server, and exercises the full `SecurityFilterChain`.
- Three setup decisions matter:
- **`@WebMvcTest`** — fast slice test; auto-configures `MockMvc` with the security filter chain via `SecurityMockMvcConfigurers.springSecurity()`.
- **Cannot test method security on services** because AOP proxies aren't created.
- **`@SpringBootTest` + `@AutoConfigureMockMvc`** — full context; method security works; slower; use when controller tests must call services that have `@PreAuthorize`.
- **`@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` + `TestRestTemplate`** — real HTTP; closest to production; use sparingly for the most critical flows (login, logout, OAuth2 callback).

**`with(csrf())`** is the single most-forgotten detail: any CSRF-enabled chain rejects POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH without a valid CSRF token.
- The test failure looks like an authorization failure (403) but is actually CSRF.
- Always include `with(csrf())` in state-changing tests on CSRF-enabled chains, and also write one explicit test that omits it to confirm CSRF protection is active.

sections.title: @WebMvcTest Setup with Security
Method Security with @SpringBootTest + @EnableMethodSecurity
Custom @WithSecurityContext Factory for JWT
Integration Tests with Testcontainers Keycloak
Test Strategy: Helps, Hurts, Watch For
sections.content:
**When `@WebMvcTest` helps:**
- Per-controller security rule testing
- Fast (no full context boot)
- Auto-configured MockMvc with security filter chain
- Easy mocking of services with `@MockBean`

**When `@SpringBootTest` is required:**
- Method-level security (`@PreAuthorize`/`@PostAuthorize`)
- Cross-controller flows that hit the real service AOP proxies
- Wiring custom `AuthenticationProvider` or `JwtDecoder`

**When Testcontainers Keycloak helps:**
- True end-to-end OAuth2/OIDC validation
- Real JWKS, signature, claims
- Catches issues mocked tokens hide

**When it hurts:**
- `@WebMvcTest` for method security -> false positives
- `@SpringBootTest` for trivial controller test -> slow suite
- Testcontainers everywhere -> CI explosion
- Skipping `with(csrf())` -> 403 misdiagnosed as authz failure

**Watch for:**
- **AOP proxies absent in `@WebMvcTest`** — `@PreAuthorize` silently no-op
- **Missing `@EnableMethodSecurity`** — annotations ignored even in `@SpringBootTest`
- **CSRF token absent** — every state-changing test fails 403; misleading
- **`@WithMockUser` for JWT endpoint** — wrong token type; ClassCastException or empty claims
- **Test mutating `SecurityContextHolder`** — clear in `@AfterEach` to avoid leakage
- **Auth via `@MockBean` on `AuthenticationManager`** — bypasses real validation; rarely what you want
- **Forgetting negative tests** — happy path passes; broken authz ships to prod
- **`@SpringBootTest` + flaky integration tests** — keep DB/Keycloak isolated per test
- **CI parallelism** — Testcontainers ports collide; use random ports and isolation

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **`@WebMvcTest` auto-applies `springSecurity()` to MockMvc** — security filter chain is wired without setup.
- **Always include `with(csrf())`** for POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH on CSRF-enabled chains; write one explicit test that omits it.
- **Method security needs `@SpringBootTest` + `@EnableMethodSecurity`** — `@WebMvcTest` does not load AOP proxies.
- **Write negative tests for every rule** — wrong role -> 403, no auth -> 401, missing CSRF -> 403.
- **Custom `@WithMockJwtUser` annotation** for JWT Resource Server tests — correct token type and reusable.
- **`SecurityMockMvcResultMatchers.authenticated().withAuthorities(...)`** asserts security context, not just HTTP status.
- **Testcontainers Keycloak** for end-to-end OAuth2 validation — sparingly for critical flows.
- **Distinguish 401 vs 403 in assertions** — 401 = no auth, 403 = authenticated but unauthorized.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**MockMvc setup**
- `@WebMvcTest(Controller.class)` + `@Import(SecurityConfig.class)`
- MockMvc auto-configured with security filter chain via `SecurityMockMvcConfigurers.springSecurity()`
- `@MockBean` for service dependencies

**Method security**
- `@SpringBootTest` (not `@WebMvcTest`) so AOP proxies are created
- `@EnableMethodSecurity` in test config
- `@WithMockUser` + `assertThrows(AccessDeniedException.class, ...)`

**CSRF**
- `with(csrf())` for state-changing requests
- Write one explicit test that omits it to verify CSRF protection is active

**JWT Resource Server**
- Use `with(jwt().jwt(jb -> jb.subject().claim(...)).authorities(...))` per request
- Or build `@WithMockJwtUser` with `WithSecurityContextFactory` for reuse

**Negative tests are first-class**
- For every `requestMatchers` rule and every `@PreAuthorize`:
  - Allowed role -> 2xx
  - Wrong role -> 403
  - No auth -> 401
  - Missing CSRF -> 403 (one canary test)

**Result matchers beyond status**
- `SecurityMockMvcResultMatchers.authenticated().withAuthorities(...)`
- Distinguishes 200 from `permitAll()` vs 200 from authenticated access

**End-to-end**
- Testcontainers Keycloak for real OAuth2 flows
- Real JWKS, signature, `iss`/`aud` validation
- Sparingly for critical flows; not every endpoint

**Common mistakes**
- `@WebMvcTest` for method security -> silent false positive
- Missing `@EnableMethodSecurity` -> annotations ignored
- Missing `with(csrf())` -> misdiagnosed 403
- `@WithMockUser` for JWT endpoints -> wrong token type
